issuer: the Virginia Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)
note: The DMV's fee form DMV 201 (dated 10 August 2026, read 2026-10-30) gives a driver's licence only at $4 a year (minimum $20), $32.00, and photo identification at $2 a year (minimum $10, maximum $16); the apply page says a licence is generally valid for up to eight years, so the licence was kept as 8 years at $32.00, and the card is kept as 8 years at $16, the maximum (the card's 8-year term is read from the $2-a-year rate reaching its $16 maximum at eight years, a reading). Code of Virginia 46.2-334.01 (read on the General Assembly's site) restricts licences issued to persons under 18, so a full licence is kept from 18. No youngest age for the card was read. On 2026-10-30 the licence was rewritten with the terms set by the holder's age: 8 years at $32.00 under 75 and 5 years at $20.00 from 75 ($4 a year times 5, which is also DMV 201's minimum). The apply page says a renewed licence lasts five years from 75; it is held for any licence issued from 75 (a reading). Until then the file held the 8-year licence only. Later on 2026-10-30 both terms were rewritten to hold DMV 201's rate, $4 for each year of the term, charged for each of its years, in place of the products ($32.00 and $20.00), which the file held until then. The $20 minimum changes neither term's charge (8 years at $4 is $32.00, above it; 5 years is $20.00, at it), so no term holds a printed charge in place of the rate.
